description: Labelled ground-truth corpus for content-quality-audit's script-decided, single-page capabilities (CQ-03/05/07/08/10/11). Clean cases carry an empty expectation on purpose: they are the false-positive control. Every clean case here was chosen because it resembles a defect closely enough to have tripped an earlier version of the detector during development — see docs/phase-4-completion-2.md for CQ-03/05/07/08 and docs/phase-4-completion-8.md for CQ-11, including one case (defect_dense_jargon_short_sentences) that was drafted as an intended 'clean' fixture and reclassified to 'defect' after it turned out to genuinely cross CQ-11's threshold — a real finding from building this corpus, not a hypothetical. CQ-10's freshness cases carry optional `headers`/`fetched_at` fields consumed by measure_content_quality.py's run_case — CQ-10's other half, cross-page fact collision, is `--sample-file` multi-page mode and not covered by this per-page harness.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Ordinary prose, a repeated-but-identical metric (not ambiguous), a correctly-computed average, and an absolutely-dated change.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Template syntax shown as a teaching example inside <pre><code>. Must be stripped before matching.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Two metrics repeated with different values, each carrying a qualifier ('up to') that explains the difference; one weighted average.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Changes anchored to absolute dates, plus relative-time phrases with no claim verb attached (must not fire on their own).

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Unrendered {{ }} and {% %} tokens in the visible page body.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Four changes described only in relative time, no absolute date in any sentence.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Two independently labeled metrics, each stated twice with different values and no qualifier. Regression fixture for the 'per' substring bug ('Warranty period' was being wrongly suppressed by a naive substring match on the qualifier word 'per').

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Two independent labeled lists whose stated averages contradict the arithmetic of their own listed numbers. Regression fixture for the singular/plural keyword-matching gap ('ratings' vs 'rating') and the parenthesised-label parsing gap ('Delivery times (days)').

cases.label: clean
cases.note: 302 words of ordinary short-sentence, plain-vocabulary prose (a typical product FAQ). The false-positive control for CQ-11: long enough to be scored, plain enough to stay well above the 'very difficult' threshold.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: 331 words of long, syllable-dense sentences (avg. 36.8 words/sentence). Scores well below the CQ-11 threshold on both axes the formula weighs.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: 309 words of short, simple medical-clinic sentences (avg. 6.9 words/sentence) built from syllable-dense clinical vocabulary. Drafted as an intended CQ-11 false-positive control and reclassified after it genuinely crossed the threshold (score 9.9) — Flesch's syllable-per-word term dominates its sentence-length term heavily enough that short sentences alone do not protect against dense jargon. See content-anti-patterns.md's CQ-11 section.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: CQ-10's single-page freshness half (cycle 23 Phase 2, B7). Visible text claims 'Last updated: August 20, 2026' but the HTTP Last-Modified header reports January 10, 2024 — over two years earlier than the page's own claim, well past the trust window and the minimum gap.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Dominant false positive for CQ-10's freshness half: the Last-Modified header is only 10 minutes before the fetch time, the CDN-stamps-serve-time signature — indistinguishable from a genuine fresh edit from a single fetch, so the check refuses to fire at all rather than guess.
